 Runtime changed-line coverage 97.87%; mapped total 88.03%; testkit 97.62%;
  backend and macro cohorts retained separately at 95.11% and 100%. 
 DID v0.7.0: 12 stateful exports; 42 finite relation calls. 
 Passport cohort: 17 files, 75 pure exports, 202 behavior cases and four
  codec vectors. Full Passport ACC adoption was removed. 
 Remote core: 742 cases in 63 result blocks at the named revision. 
 RustSec: zero vulnerability matches, with four workspace / three standalone
  notices and strict nonzero exit retained. 
 
 Counts overlap and must not be summed into one “tests passed” figure. 
 Effect prototype — active local program 
 At  f3cef799 , the saved story cutoff includes the historical-test process
sharding change. The full installed validation kept 974 unique planned and
executed IDs with no failures, errors, skips or unrun cases. Four independent
process shards reduced the measured wall time from 10,270 seconds (about
171 minutes) to 3,308 seconds (about 55 minutes), a 3.105× result on this
frozen machine and source. 
 What remained unchanged matters more than the headline: 
 
 the original 940 cases and their assertions remained; 
 workers reconstructed independent temporary state; 
 live source/manifest mutation checks still ran; 
 original case IDs and accounting remained exact; 
 eight new corruption/source controls lived outside frozen discovery; 
 no validation result cache or live path cache was introduced. 
 
 It is a measured local optimization, not a universal CI speed claim. 
 Parity findings that changed the design 
 The TypeScript comparison was not a ceremonial check. It found genuine Rust
divergences, including incorrect hash-to-curve representation, the wrong
Jubjub Schnorr predicate, permissive Boolean/bounded-unsigned decoding, and a
validated-point alias that could panic for attacker-controlled coordinates. 
 Rust also found genuine source/runtime defects: malformed native widths that
JS silently sliced, and Merkle update underflow before a capacity check. The
right conclusion is not “Rust won.” Independent implementations made hidden
assumptions observable in both directions. 
 Current limitations 
 
 No formal proof of complete Compact semantics or universal TS parity. 
 Proof support is per applicable export and exact artifact set. 
 The effect prototype is local and not yet EA13-closed. 
 Source locations at the cutoff are owner locations plus structural paths,
  not complete nested ranges. 
 Aggregate decoded heap/object/CPU containment remains separate work. 
 Experimental WASM does not imply a production browser prover. 
 No Windows certification, package registry release or upstream adoption is
  implied by the closed local/fork milestones.

title: Read the generated Rust
Runtime and macro ownership
text:
Historical atlas. This chapter preserves the October 14 documentation cutoff. The main narrative records subsequent deliveries and current limits. 
 Source snapshot —  original chapter at 51a079bd . The documented implementation cutoff is f3cef799 on October 14. The documentation snapshot and implementation revision are distinct. 
 
 The Rust backend is not one generated file. It is a set of ownership
boundaries. The most useful mental model is a transition from a source-owned
contract to a ledger-owned call, with the runtime carrying typed evidence
between them. 
 Domain map 
  generated contract
  ├─ types ─────────────── derives ────── FAB / field / binary representation
  ├─ ledger_slots ──────── typed path ─── canonical ledger-8 VM operation
  ├─ Witnesses ─────────── private step ─ private state + private FAB output
  ├─ native circuit ────── CircuitFrame / CircuitResult
  └─ recorded circuit ──── RecordingFrame / RecordedCircuitResult
                                      │
                                      ▼
observation ── RecordedCall ── replay + partition ── ContractCallPrototype
                                                       │
                                  verifier/prover/ledger application
  
 Core execution types 
 
 
 
 Type 
 Owns 
 Must not be mistaken for 
 
 
 
 
  ConstructorContext<Private>  
 Initial private state, wallet-local Zswap state and source-ordered circuit intents 
 A deployed ledger contract 
 
 
  ConstructorResult<Private>  
 Constructed charged ledger state plus private/Zswap successors 
 Proof or deployment evidence 
 
 
  CircuitContext<Private>  
 Private state, upstream  QueryContext , cost model, per-query gas limit, Zswap plan and optional execution key 
 A replayable trace 
 
 
  WitnessContext  
 Borrowed private state, typed ledger view and contract address 
 Permission to disclose witness values 
 
 
  WitnessReadMeter  
 Canonical VM reads made through witness projections and their observed cost 
 A public verifying operation 
 
 
  CircuitResult<Private, Output>  
 Successor context, source result, summed query gas and private FAB outputs 
 A proof-ready transaction 
 
 
  CircuitFrame  
 Ordered native composition of nested calls, witness steps and their costs/outputs 
 A procedural macro or compiler IR 
 
 
 
  CircuitContext.gas_limit  is a ledger-8 limit applied to each individual VM
query.  CircuitResult.gas_cost  is the accumulated diagnostic cost of accepted
queries. A whole-circuit budget is not implied. 
 Primitive ownership map 
 The facade is deliberately thin. It preserves Compact names and checked
conversion points while keeping the ledger-8 types authoritative: 
 
 
 
 Compact surface 
 Rust runtime facade 
 Ledger / ZK authority 
 
 
 
 
  Field  
  runtime::Field  /  runtime::Fr  
 Alias of  midnight_transient_crypto::curve::Fr  
 
 
  Bytes<N> ,  Vector<N,T>  
  FixedBytes<N> ,  FixedVector<T,N>  with FAB and field/binary representations 
  midnight_base_crypto::fab::{AlignedValue, Value, Alignment}  plus  midnight_transient_crypto::repr  
 
 
  Cell ,  Set ,  Map ,  List , Merkle declarations 
 Typed  *Slot  values and  CircuitContext  operations 
  midnight_onchain_runtime::QueryContext ,  midnight_onchain_vm::Op ,  midnight_onchain_state::StateValue , and storage collections 
 
 
 Coin information, recipient and shielded intents 
 Conversion helpers plus  CircuitZswapPlan  
  midnight_coin_structure  and  midnight_zswap  
 
 
  JubjubPoint , hashes and commitments 
 Checked  JubjubPoint  wrapper and native functions 
  midnight_transient_crypto  plus checked decoding through  midnight_curves  
 
 
 Recorded call and verifier material 
  RecordedCall  to  ContractCallPrototype  
  midnight_ledger  transaction construction; proof providers use the pinned  midnight-proofs  /  midnight-zkir  graph 
 
 
 
 The last row is a boundary rather than a type alias. Generated code creates a
typed recorded call and enters preparation. It does not hide proving or ledger
application inside emitted syntax. The proof testkit uses
 midnight_zkir::LocalProvingProvider ; the runtime transaction adapter binds
 VerifierKey  and  ProofPreimage  from the ledger's transient-crypto graph. 
  generated types ── FAB / FieldRepr ── ledger value representation
typed slots ────── checked VM ops ─── QueryContext + StateValue
Zswap intents ─── explicit binding ── Offer + ledger Zswap state
recorded call ─── replay/partition ── ContractCallPrototype
                                          │
                              provider proves / ledger applies
  
 Ledger slots 
 The generated declaration fixes a value type and a physical path. Runtime slot
types expose only operations appropriate to that declaration: 
 
 
 
 Slot 
 Representative operations 
 
 
 
 
  CellSlot<T>  
 typed read/write, local inspection, witness read, recorded read/write 
 
 
  CounterSlot  
 increment/decrement, less-than query, witness and recorded forms 
 
 
  SetSlot<T>  
 insert/remove/member/size/is-empty with structural and metered views 
 
 
  MapSlot<K,V>  
 typed key/value operations; nested  MapNode  distinguishes non-scalar values 
 
 
  ListSlot<T>  
 push/pop/head/length with declared physical path 
 
 
  MerkleSlot<T, DEPTH, HISTORIC>  
 typed leaves, declared depth and compile-time historic capability 
 
 
 
 Slots prevent the generator from rebuilding VM opcodes for every contract.
They do not make arbitrary paths valid: runtime builders still check operand
width, root/reset semantics, alignment and upstream query rejection. 
 Recording domain 
  RecordingFrame  executes admitted operations while retaining two products: 
 
  CircuitResult  — what native execution did, including private outputs and
   observed query gas; 
  PublicTrace  — initial public context plus ordered ledger-8 Verify
   operations and sealed execution/Zswap identities. 
 
  RecordedCircuitResult  pairs those products without claiming that replay,
proof or transaction preparation has succeeded. 
 Transaction domain 
 
 
 
 Type 
 Boundary it authenticates 
 
 
 
 
  Observation  
 Caller-supplied transaction/block identity; explicitly not finality proof 
 
 
  ObservedContractState  
 Address + public contract + observation + allocation/execution identity policy 
 
 
  RecordedCall  
 Recorded trace + source entry point + typed FAB input + originating observed state 
 
 
  CallSpec  
 Exact verifier, key location, entry point, public input and commitment randomness 
 
 
  ContractCallPrototype  
 Replayed and partitioned ledger call ready for later proving/transaction construction 
 
 
 
 Preparation checks address, initial state, execution key, installed operation
and verifier identity before replay/partition. Errors such as
 StateMismatch ,  VerifierMismatch ,  ReplayEffectsMismatch  and
 PartitionEffectsMismatch  are trust-boundary failures rather than Compact
source type errors. 
 The evidence flow is intentionally longer than a generated function call: 
  Generate          Execute          Record             Prepare
types + slots  -> CircuitResult -> RecordedResult  -> ContractCallPrototype
                                                           |
                                                           v
Apply          <- Verify/prove  <- ProofPreimage + exact artifact identity
Intent/Tx          provider          provider / ZKIR / parameters
  
 Each arrow can fail independently. This is why native execution, recording,
preparation, proof verification and ledger application are reported as
different capabilities. 
 Shielded intent domain 
  CircuitZswapPlan  records ordered circuit input/output intents and allocation
state. Its output indices can be provisional during native execution or exact
when bound to an authoritative offer. It is deliberately separate from wallet
state and from a validated offer. 
 What the macros own 
 The proc-macro crate is intentionally narrow: 
 
 
 
 Macro 
 Mechanical responsibility 
 
 
 
 
  CompactCellValue  
 FAB alignment/conversion and checked Cell decoding 
 
 
  CompactEnum  
 Default first variant, checked ordinal, field and binary representations 
 
 
  CompactStructRepr  
 Fully qualified delegation of field/binary representations for named concrete structs 
 
 
  CompactMerkleTreeDigest ,  CompactMerklePathEntry ,  CompactMerklePath  
 Mechanical Merkle representation glue 
 
 
  compact_witness_bridge  
 Generate fallible  TryWitnesses  and the infallible adapter from one visible trait 
 
 
 
 Macros do  not  decide Compact control flow, recording admission, ledger
paths, disclosure, gas policy or proof support. Those stay in the frontend,
typed backend and runtime respectively. This boundary follows
 RUST-ADR-0004 ,
 RUST-ADR-0005 
and  RUST-ADR-0038 . 
 Compatibility boundaries 
 At the documented head, generated code asserts runtime ABI 50 at compile time.
The Chez-to-Rust private IR is schema 20 and the capability report is schema 3.
Those numbers describe different internal contracts and must not be compared
as one version line. The runtime reuses ledger-8.0.3 primitives; a matching ABI
does not by itself establish proof keys, network compatibility or application
adoption.

title: Gas, errors and corrected boundaries
text:
Historical atlas. This chapter preserves the October 14 documentation cutoff. The main narrative records subsequent deliveries and current limits. 
 Source snapshot —  original chapter at 51a079bd . The documented implementation cutoff is f3cef799 on October 14. The documentation snapshot and implementation revision are distinct. 
 
 The backend became more trustworthy by moving failures to the earliest layer
that has enough information to explain them—without pretending every failure
can happen at compile time. 
 The gas-accounting correction 
 The original comparison looked alarming: Rust reported much more gas than the
TypeScript wrapper for the same  tiny  circuit. The implementations were not
using the same reporting denominator. 
 TypeScript replaced  context.gasCost  after each query and exposed the last
query. Generated Rust accumulated every query. The accepted decision in
 RUST-ADR-0010 
kept the Rust total and changed the comparison to the sum of captured
TypeScript query costs. For  clear ,  set  and  get , all four dimensions then
matched exactly at commit
  3799746a  . 
  reported TS wrapper cost       = last query only
captured TS comparison cost    = Σ every executed query
Rust CircuitResult.gas_cost    = Σ every executed query
transaction gas                = replay/partition result, separately owned
  
 The four dimensions are read time, compute time, bytes written and bytes
deleted. They should not be collapsed into one scalar. 
 Witness reads became visible 
 A witness could read a ledger Cell structurally while TypeScript executed a VM
read. Rust therefore underreported the call. The explicit  WitnessReadMeter 
introduced at
  98d33ca7  
charges canonical witness projection queries while keeping their private value
out of the public trace. The Set extension followed at
  2ca64f6f  . 
 One witnessed Cell write moved from an incomplete Rust read-time total of
85,000,000 to the exact captured total of 255,000,000: 170,000,000 for the
witness read plus 85,000,000 for the write. That is corrected accounting, not
a cheaper VM operation. 
 Per-query guard, whole-circuit observation 
 At ledger-8,  CircuitContext.gas_limit  guards each query independently. A
circuit containing two accepted reads may therefore report a total above the
configured one-query limit. Commit
  7c489892  
made that contract explicit and tested. Silently turning it into a cumulative
budget would diverge from the pinned TypeScript/ledger behavior and introduce
new rollback questions. 
 Compile-time versus runtime failures 
 
 
 
 Layer 
 Example 
 Why it belongs there 
 
 
 
 
 Compact frontend 
 Type mismatch, invalid disclosure or source recursion 
 The source language has complete typing/scope information 
 
 
 Private IR admission 
 Unknown schema node, recursive direct IR call, invalid declaration reference 
 Prevent malformed or forged compiler input from reaching emission 
 
 
 Rust backend 
 Emitted-name collision, unsupported wide operation, incomplete recording capability 
 Target naming and backend capability are known before publication 
 
 
 Proc macro / rustc 
 Data-carrying  CompactEnum , hostile introduced name, wrong witness impl signature 
 The error is a Rust representation/consumer integration defect 
 
 
 Native runtime 
 Failed Compact assertion, unsigned overflow, invalid ledger Cell, rejected VM query 
 Depends on call values or ledger state 
 
 
 Recording 
 Unsupported complete effect plan, replay-visible invariant failure 
 Native execution may exist while complete recording does not 
 
 
 Preparation 
 Address/state/verifier mismatch, empty transcript, unbound Zswap intent 
 Requires observed state and exact artifacts 
 
 
 Ledger/prover 
 Invalid proof, unsatisfied transaction policy, application refusal 
 Owned by authoritative proof and ledger validation 
 
 
 
 Representative issues that were fixed 
 Invalid Rust became a source-located compiler error 
 Distinct Compact circuit names such as  a$b  and  a_b  normalize to the same
Rust identifier. Before, rustc rejected a duplicated function after emission.
Commit
  c70dd63c  
added target-namespace preflight and reports both source names at the later
declaration. See  RUST-ADR-0246 . 
 Macro expansion stopped depending on caller names 
 Derives introduced unqualified  Result ,  Option ,  Vec  and  From , so valid
consumer names could break compilation. Commit
  77c9ee14  
fully qualified macro-owned names. Source structs named  Option ,  Fr ,
 MemWrite ,  runtime  or  FieldRepr  exposed a second failure in upstream
derive/import expansion; the owned  CompactStructRepr  boundary fixed the
bounded generated shapes at
  ee768a60  . 
 Forged recursive IR stopped becoming recursive Rust 
 The normal frontend rejected recursive Compact, but direct schema-20 IR could
still emit recursive pure Rust. Commit
  dbfd7dc2  
moved the refusal to private-IR semantic admission while preserving acyclic
shared helpers. See  RUST-ADR-0332 . 
 Malformed ledger paths stopped panicking or truncating 
 Merkle/list reset builders used  split_last().expect ; other builders narrowed
path lengths before constructing compact VM operands. Commit
  e6807884  
checks the actual 4-bit  Ins / Idx  encoding limits and returns the existing
fallible ledger error rather than panicking, truncating or emitting an
ambiguous program. See  RUST-ADR-0351 . 
 A truthful refusal replaced a misleading bounds error 
 Valid wide unsigned types could be represented, but subtraction,
multiplication and ordered comparison were unsupported. They were incorrectly
reported as malformed maxima. Commit
  6aa345fd  
added  UnsupportedWideUnsignedOperation  without widening accepted behavior.
See  RUST-ADR-0352 . 
 The architectural rule 
 Move a failure earlier only when the earlier layer has authoritative facts.
Source recursion and name collisions belong before Rust publication. An
assertion depending on current ledger state remains a runtime  Result .
Verifier identity cannot be authenticated until preparation. Proof and ledger
rejection must not be simulated by compiler heuristics.

title: The original decision ledger
text:
Editorial correction for this edition. The ACC-removal rationale below is superseded by ADR 0316. The owner removed ACC after the construct inventory found no unique witness, struct or ledger mechanisms. Its exact application composition was unqualified. The later narrative uses that recorded reason. 
 Historical atlas. This chapter preserves the October 14 documentation cutoff. The main narrative records subsequent deliveries and current limits. 
 Source snapshot —  original chapter at 51a079bd . The documented implementation cutoff is f3cef799 on October 14. The documentation snapshot and implementation revision are distinct. 
 
 The useful history is not a straight line. These are representative moments
where the evidence changed the architecture or narrowed a claim. 
 1. Preserve the old backend instead of deleting it 
  Problem.  A clean rewrite could regress behavior while making comparison
impossible. 
  Decision.  Keep  codegen-rust  as an oracle and compare exact sources,
results, state, transcripts and refusals. 
  Evidence.  The first Rust-AST milestone ran all 37 exact top-level oracle
sources through the new path. 
  Benefit.  The project could change the architecture without rewriting its
own history. 
  Limit.  An oracle can contain defects; agreement is evidence, not truth. 
 2. Use a closed IR, not a Rust-source escape hatch 
  Problem.  Text fragments let unsupported source shapes leak into output and
made exhaustive review difficult. 
  Decision.  Model Compact types, expressions, actions and returns as strict
serde variants and reject unknown input. 
  Evidence.  Compiler-backed refusal probes, fixture regeneration and external
Cargo consumers accompanied schema changes. 
  Benefit.  New constructs require an explicit compiler/backend decision. 
  Limit.  The private schema still couples the Chez producer and Rust consumer;
its version is not a public language specification. 
 3. Generated syntax is necessary, not sufficient 
  Problem.   syn  guarantees parseable Rust construction, but semantic bugs
can still live inside valid syntax. 
  Decision.  Keep AST construction and add execution, independent expected
values, TypeScript observations, negative controls, replay and proof gates. 
  Evidence.  Field modular arithmetic, Boolean witness order, source-defined
returns and output-recovery tests caught stale or overly textual assumptions. 
  Benefit.  Generated code is checked as a program, not a string. 
  Limit.  Hundreds of substring assertions remain useful smoke tests but are
not semantic proof. 
 4. The point type was too “safe” 
  Problem.  Rust represented Compact  JubjubPoint  as a validated subgroup
point. Compact's source value is a coordinate pair, and the upstream constructor
could panic on some invalid/subgroup-external coordinates. 
  Decision.  Separate source representation from checked operation admission;
validate only where an operation requires a real point. 
  Evidence.  Cross-language parity tests reproduced the divergent values and
panic boundary. 
  Benefit.  Rust no longer changes source representation under the banner of
type safety. 
  Limit.  A checked backend may still deliberately refuse behavior that the
reference path accepts; that difference must be documented, not hidden. 
 5. Shape recognizers reached their ceiling 
  Problem.  Every useful application family added another whole-program
admission profile. Supported operations did not compose automatically. 
  Decision.  Introduce a typed  RecordedPlan , migrate one family at a time,
and retain the old paths as differential oracles until retirement evidence
exists. 
  Evidence.  Per-family default/feature tests, generated-source inventories,
source-bound proof/application cases and an explicit retirement ledger. 
  Benefit.  The unit of reuse becomes an operation plus its invariants. 
  Limit.  A compositional IR can centralize bugs too; exhaustive variants,
resource limits and old-first laws remain necessary. 
 6. Full Passport ACC adoption was the wrong milestone goal 
  Problem.  A large ledger9-era application risked turning unrelated foreign
curve, WebAuthn and newer-ledger requirements into alleged ledger-8 support. 
  Decision.  Inventory constructs, retain generic Jubjub work, remove full ACC
adoption and keep bounded passport/DID cohorts separately evidenced. 
  Evidence.  The 0.3 closure records the removed outcome and the exact retained
application cases. 
  Benefit.  Useful compiler work survived without a misleading product claim. 
  Limit.  The bounded passport cohort is not the full ACC application. 
 7. A faster test gate may not skip authentication 
  Problem.  Historical validation took about 171 minutes, more than 99% in
historical checks. Naive memoization would have hidden live mutation. 
  Decision.  Reject path/result caches and shard whole modules into isolated
processes, preserving fixture boundaries and independent temporary state. 
  Evidence.  All 974 IDs and assertions remained; corruption and source
mutation controls passed; measured wall time fell to about 55 minutes. 
  Benefit.  Faster feedback without turning a historical assurance suite into
a snapshot replay. 
  Limit.  The result is machine/source specific and still needs the full gate
at final freeze. 
 8. Source provenance must be honest 
  Problem.  Hand-built IR can make a backend look more source-compatible than
the frontend actually is, while absolute paths and private artifacts are unsafe
to publish. 
  Decision.  Authenticate source, IR and artifact sidecars; distinguish
original occurrences, owned snapshots and missing origins; carry safe logical
source identity and structural paths. 
  Evidence.  Authenticated input views, original-source guards and publication
manifests preserve exact hashes and failure cases. 
  Benefit.  A passing fixture can be tied back to a real Compact source. 
  Limit.  Nested expression ranges and transient-value provenance are not
claimed implemented at this cutoff. 
 Independent review boundary 
 The project used independent coding-agent reviews for architecture, dependency,
correctness and final-slice checks. They found actionable issues and provided a
useful second model. They are not a human security audit, formal verification
or production certification. The story uses the exact phrase “independent
coding-agent review” for that reason.

title: A working glossary
text:
Historical atlas. This chapter preserves the October 14 documentation cutoff. The main narrative records subsequent deliveries and current limits. 
 Source snapshot —  original chapter at 51a079bd . The documented implementation cutoff is f3cef799 on October 14. The documentation snapshot and implementation revision are distinct. 
 
  Compact 
Midnight's smart-contract language and compiler pipeline. 
  Chez Scheme 
The implementation language of the Compact frontend and compiler passes used
here. It remains responsible for parsing, typing and shared analysis. 
  Rust-AST backend 
The target that consumes a private typed IR and constructs Rust syntax through
 syn ,  quote ,  proc-macro2  and  prettyplease . 
  Private IR 
The versioned JSON interchange between Chez and the Rust renderer. Its schema
version is internal; it is not a Compact language specification version. 
  FAB / aligned value 
The field-aligned binary/value representation used across Compact values,
witness transcripts and ledger/proof boundaries. 
  Native execution 
Running a generated circuit against the Rust runtime to obtain a result and
updated context. It does not imply recording or proof support. 
  Recording 
Producing the ordered public VM/effect program and private/public values needed
for replay and later proof-oriented integration. 
  Replay 
Checking a recorded program against observed state and runtime invariants. 
  Preparation 
Constructing a ledger call/prototype from recorded execution, observed state,
verifier material and caller-supplied policy. 
  Proof applicability 
Whether a circuit and its exact artifacts have the required public/private
inputs and policy to be proved. A generated recording API is not enough. 
  Shape recognizer / recording profile 
A specialized admission path that recognizes a known whole-circuit pattern.
It was useful for early coverage but did not compose naturally. 
  Recording effect algebra 
The prototype's typed vocabulary and composition rules for building a complete
 RecordedPlan  from checked operations. 
  Typed refusal /  RecordingGap  
A structured explanation that native code may exist while a complete recorded
path does not. It carries a stable code, node, structural path and detail. 
  Oracle 
An independent implementation or captured output used for comparison. Oracles
are evidence and can themselves contain bugs. 
  Old-first law 
A migration check that asks the legacy implementation first, then ensures the
new path preserves accepted/refused behavior and takes ownership deliberately. 
  CoPS 
Compact problem statements that record cross-component issues without
pretending a local workaround is an upstream specification decision. 
  ADR 
Architecture Decision Record: problem, decision, alternatives, ownership,
evidence and limitations at a named point in history.
